text:
miguel: quick heads-up — seeing a ~60-150ms p95 blip on long-context jobs (>32k tokens) starting ~2h ago. KV evicter rate jumped ~3x.
priya: can you paste the evicter metrics and a short perf profile? LRU or FIFO paths?
miguel: attaching quick snapshot — looks like LRU churn.
```
evicter.rate: 1200/s -> 3600/s
kv.reuse.hit_rate: 0.72 -> 0.41
pager.io_ops: +2.6x
p95_latency_tokens: 420ms -> 540ms
```
priya: ugh. reuse hit rate dropping that much would explain token regen cost. did we recently change the hotset watermark or sampling window?
dan: not in config. last change was kernel selection tweak to prefer async kernels for attention when seq>16k.
zoe: also saw increased memory growth in a few hosts, paging kicked in, and some threads reported `OOM-like` reclaim churn.
alice: could be an interaction: async kernels change the request ordering and extend KV live times, shifting the working set and provoking eviction storms.
miguel: I ran a quick perf top on one host — shows heavy time in `evicter::evict_batch` and a spike in `kv::insert_retain` locking.
```
# perf script trimmed
  24.3% evicter::evict_batch
  12.7% kv::insert_retain
   9.1% kernel::async_attention_loop
```
priya: interesting — eviction hot path + insert lock. That suggests reinsert-after-evict races. When an inflight request reuses a chunk but eviction already queued it, we might be doing a full reinsert rather than a cheap reuse.
dan: could repro locally with a long-context replay harness? I can try setting seq_len=48k and hammer with variable batch sizes.
infra-bot: started job `evict-repro/1757654321-1` on staging cluster (3 nodes, seq=48k, mix=rand(8-64)).
zoe: if it's LRU-specific we should also test FIFO variant and probabilistic evict to see latency differences.
alice: agree — let's run LRU vs FIFO vs hybrid with the same workload, collect reuse hit_rate, pager ops, and p95. I'll script it.
miguel: quick mitigation for prod: enable small prefix-KV lock window and raise hotset watermark by +10% to reduce evicter pressure. rolling patch in canary now.
priya: good. once we have repro, we should add a unit/integration test that asserts no reinsert-after-evict doubles work (i.e., `evict()` and immediate `insert()` should be observable as a single transition).
dan: note: batching heuristics can hide this — smaller batches increase evict frequency, larger batches increase KV live size. we'll need to test multiple batchers.
zoe: also log lines to add: `evict_reason`, `reinsert_source`, and `batch_id` so we can correlate. lightweight boolean flags to avoid perf hit.
alice: agreed. created a GH issue with checklist and perf artifacts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evicter/issues/412
miguel: can we also surface a temporary alert on reuse_hit_rate < 0.6 to catch regressions earlier?
priya: setting alert in metrics now (staging threshold 0.5, prod 0.65).
infra-bot: canary rollout for hotset-watermark bump: 2/5 pods healthy, rolling.
miguel: after bump, initial look: reuse_hit_rate up to 0.61 and p95 back down ~30-40ms. holding to confirm.
priya: great — next steps: 1) repro harness for LRU/FIFO/hybrid + batch sweep, 2) add lightweight telemetry for evict/reinsert correlation, 3) test with async kernel selection on/off to confirm ordering hypothesis.
dan: i'll own the repro harness and baseline numbers.
zoe: i'll add telemetry and alert.
alice: i'll draft the post on root-cause and permanent fixes once we have repro.
miguel: thanks team. tagging folks to follow up: @priya @dan @zoe @alice :thumbsup:
